caption: The drawing depicts a section of an interior wall, featuring an arched architectural niche at the center with a rounded, recessed cavity beneath an ornately decorated arch outlined in red and blue. The wall is adorned with geometric patterns and symbols primarily in red tones, with accent colors of blue and brown. To the left of the niche is a circular motif filled with concentric rings and lines, connected to a U-shaped red vessel-like shape hanging below it, positioned above a triangular element. Above the central niche and extending slightly to the left and right are two additional arches, embellished with alternating red and blue decorations. A horizontal band at mid-wall level features alternating red shapes and small red crosses. The surface beneath the niche displays a repeating diamond pattern in faded red and white, and the ground is drawn with reddish-brown rectangular tiles arranged in rows. The overall appearance is weathered, with visible patches and stains on both floor and wall. The artist's name, "Juanita Donahoo," is signed at the lower right corner.
title: Wall Painting and Baptismal Niche
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
